findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Realign the leaf to parent 708d's 'DC wiki codec (capability only)' charter: implement the segmenting renderer BEHIND `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` and set `normalize_outbound = decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` (law-consistent) in THIS story — delivering the codec half of AC2 — rather than shipping a codec-detached pure module and deferring all codec wiring to 3388 (whose parent role is only to wire an already-capable codec into the live send).
evidence: Parent 708d: 'DC wiki codec (capability only) — implement `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`: split body into blocks/list-items, render structurally-safe units to wiki via pinned `pypandoc-binary` ... set `normalize_outbound = decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` so the codec law holds; identity-passthrough fallback when pandoc is absent. ... Delivers the codec half of AC2.'
Parent 708d assigns the WIRING (not the capability) to the cutover sibling: 'Live cutover + state echo suppression ... wire the capable Cloud and DC codecs into the live send'.
Plan under review: 'this story delivers only the pure renderer module and its tests, and leaves `WikiTextCodec` fully identity.'
Plan under review §Approach: `render_markdown_to_wiki` 'is not referenced by any codec op or live send path in this story ... ready for `3388` to wire into `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`.'

Plan under review §Out of scope: 'Wiring `render_markdown_to_wiki` into `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`, redefining `normalize_outbound` to the compare form ... + the codec-law test for the rendering codec' are owned by 3388.

Contrast: the leaf's own compiled description (271c) matches the parent — it implements `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` and sets law-consistent `normalize_outbound` — so the divergence is introduced by the PLAN TEXT under review.
findings.finding: The plan under review reduces the leaf to a standalone pure `render_markdown_to_wiki` module and keeps `WikiTextCodec` fully identity, deferring the `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` wiring, the `normalize_outbound = decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` redefinition, and the codec-law re-establishment to sibling story `3388`. The parent epic `708d` explicitly assigns those codec deliverables to THIS child ('DC wiki codec (capability only) — implement `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` ... set `normalize_outbound = decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` so the codec law holds ... Delivers the codec half of AC2'), while `3388`'s parent-defined role is only to 'wire the capable ... codecs into the live send' — i.e. to consume an already-capable codec, not to create the capability. The plan therefore redefines a parent-specified deliverable and reassigns the codec-capability creation to a sibling, stepping outside the parent's contract.
findings.location: Plan §'Why this story ships a pure module, not a codec change' / §Approach / §'Explicitly OUT of scope' (vs parent 708d 'Child responsibilities → DC wiki codec (capability only)')
scenarios: When 3388 is planned/executed it must both create the codec capability AND wire it live, though the parent scoped it only to wiring an already-capable codec — the 'codec half of AC2' has no child that delivers it under this plan's split.

A reviewer verifying parent AC2 ('DC descriptions ... render to wiki for structurally-safe content while remaining echo-safe') finds the codec seam still identity after this leaf merges, with the codec deliverable pushed to a sibling not chartered for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt the leaf's own compiled description (271c): deliver `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` delegating to `wiki_render.py`, set `normalize_outbound = decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` for codec-law consistency, keep only the LIVE send-site wiring (`outbound_mapper.py:77`, `backend.py:70`) + convergence proof + rollback in 3388. If the author genuinely intends the codec to stay identity here, update the parent 708d first so its 'DC wiki codec' bullet no longer assigns `to_wire`/`normalize_outbound` to this child (which re-stales the parent's plan-review), then re-review this leaf against the corrected parent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the per-unit pandoc-error behavior (e.g. a failing unit passes through verbatim while other units still render, vs. whole-body identity on any pandoc error).
evidence: The pipeline renders per-unit, but the fallback rule is phrased at whole-body granularity.
Signal (5) unstated constraint: per-segment error behavior of a subprocess invocation.
findings.finding: The pandoc fallback is specified only for whole-body absence/error ('render_markdown_to_wiki returns the input unchanged'); it is unstated whether a pandoc error on ONE segment falls back for that unit only or aborts the whole body to identity.
findings.location: Approach — 'if pandoc is absent or errors, render_markdown_to_wiki returns the input unchanged'
scenarios: pandoc succeeds on 5 blocks but errors on block 6 — does the whole body become identity, or just block 6 passthrough?
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that a pandoc error on an individual unit falls that unit back to verbatim passthrough (echo-safe), while pandoc-absent triggers whole-body identity; log once in each case.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact pass condition for test_dc_corpus_coverage (e.g. bodies-rich ≥ 65% AND chars-rich ≥ 75%, with a stated tolerance) instead of an '≈' target.
evidence: 'rich output for ≈68% of bodies / ≈78% of chars with zero prose corruption; verified by test_dc_corpus_coverage'
The sibling regression counts are stated precisely (179 code-arrow: 0 rewrites; 70 tables: 70/70 stable) but the coverage figure uses '≈', which is not an assertable bound.
findings.finding: The corpus-coverage acceptance criterion asserts an approximate target ('≈68% of bodies / ≈78% of chars') without a concrete pass threshold or tolerance band, so test_dc_corpus_coverage has no deterministic assertion condition.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Over the vendored tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/ ... rich output for ≈68% of bodies / ≈78% of chars'
scenarios: An implementer must decide whether 67.2% passes or fails test_dc_corpus_coverage.
Fixture edits shift coverage by 1-2% and the test flaps with no defined margin.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace '≈68%/≈78%' with a concrete lower bound the test asserts, e.g. 'bodies_rich_fraction >= 0.65 and chars_rich_fraction >= 0.75'.

findings.finding: The `pypandoc-binary` wheel pin in this story and story `5c0e`'s planned version+sha-pinned, CI-cached pandoc binary (explicitly 'the way `acli` already is') are two different delivery mechanisms for the same binary; `acli` in this repo is a system prerequisite, not a pip dependency (pyproject.toml:70-71), so the two dependent stories may end up shipping pandoc two ways.
findings.location: Approach → 'pandoc delivery (portability)'; Scope → 'pyproject.toml — pinned pypandoc-binary extra'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the pandoc-availability probe's storage (module-level memo vs per-call), its idempotency, and thread-safety so the 'probe once' cache has defined ownership across the remote-MCP server shape.
evidence: Plan: 'The renderer probes pandoc availability once; if pandoc is absent or errors, render_markdown_to_wiki returns the input unchanged'
No statement of where the probe result is memoized (module global vs per-call), nor of thread-safety under a concurrent remote-MCP server shape
findings.finding: The plan introduces a module-level 'probe pandoc availability once' cache but does not specify where this cached state lives, its ownership, or its behavior under concurrent first-call (two threads/consumers probing simultaneously in an MCP-server shape).
findings.location: Approach — pandoc delivery (portability): 'The renderer probes pandoc availability once'
findings.suggested_fix: State that the probe result is a module-level idempotent memo whose worst-case concurrent behavior is a harmless re-probe (same deterministic result), or compute it per-call.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the pandoc VERSION the renderer targets (e.g. pin pandoc 3.9 alongside `pypandoc-binary`, or state a min-version) and note that `-t jira` / `-f commonmark` / `--wrap=none` were confirmed against `pandoc --help` for that version, so the ≈68%/≈78%/179/70 acceptance counts are reproducible against a known pandoc rather than whatever the wheel happens to bundle.
evidence: Plan: 'render ... to wiki via pinned `pandoc` (`-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none`)' — the exact writer/reader/flag names are asserted, not shown verified against `pandoc --help`/docs.

Plan pins only the package: 'pyproject.toml — pinned `pypandoc-binary` extra'; no pandoc binary version is stated. 'GPL/SBOM compliance for the bundled binary is handled by the robustness story `5c0e`' — and 5c0e is where version+sha pinning lives.

The `jira` writer output and `--wrap=none` behavior are pandoc-version-sensitive, and the reproducible counts (≈68%/≈78%, 179 code-arrow bodies, 70 erosion bodies) are all measured through pandoc — so an unpinned pandoc makes those AC counts version-coupled.

EVIDENCE CLASS: Partially-verified — sibling ticket 5c0e empirically confirms pandoc was run ('pandoc 3.9 exposes no --server/daemon, confirmed'; measured ~0.3s/field spawn; a 13.5-min hang), so the integration exists and the version in play was 3.9, but this plan does not record that version or a --help/flag confirmation for the jira writer surface.

Tooling note: `resolve_symbol('pypandoc')` and `('pypandoc_binary')` both returned UNRESOLVED in this environment — not disproof, but the surface is not independently verifiable from the review tools.
findings.finding: The plan asserts a specific pandoc CLI surface (`-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none`) but records no pandoc version pin and no flag-level verification note in THIS story; the pypandoc-binary bundled pandoc version is unpinned here (version+sha pinning is explicitly deferred to 5c0e), while this story's coverage/arrow/table acceptance tests run against that bundled pandoc.
findings.location: Approach (pure renderer module) → pandoc pipeline flags; pandoc delivery (portability); Acceptance Criteria (coverage/arrow/table)
scenarios: The pypandoc-binary wheel resolves to a different pandoc version in CI/prod than the one the 68%/78%/179/70 figures were measured on, and the jira writer output or --wrap=none behavior differs, making test_dc_corpus_coverage / test_dc_table_noformat_stable flap or drift.
A future pandoc renames or changes a flag's semantics; the renderer still runs but silently produces different wiki output than the pinned counts assume.
findings.suggested_fix: In the pandoc-delivery paragraph, pin (or floor) the bundled pandoc version explicitly and add a one-line note that the three flags were observed from `pandoc <ver> --help`; alternatively state that the corpus-count ACs are asserted against that exact pinned pandoc so they stay hermetic even before 5c0e adds the version+sha CI check.

findings.finding: The 'historical corpus' backing the ~68%/~78% coverage AC and the 179/70 regression counts is never located as a repo/test artifact, so its in-session evaluability and fixture validity are unknowable.
findings.location: Testing → 'Corpus coverage/safety'; AC 'Over the historical corpus … ≈68% … ≈78%'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope line naming the fixture path (e.g. tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/) and confirm the corpus is vendored into the repo, not fetched from a live environment.

findings.finding: The plan claims 'no observable DC behavior changes on merge' because outbound_mapper.py:77 and backend.py:70 are untouched, but outbound_mapper.py:77 calls normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value)) — and this story changes normalize_outbound from identity to a rendering transform, so the live DC description-send value flowing to update_issue changes on merge even with line 77 physically unedited.
findings.location: Scope boundary paragraph + 'Explicitly OUT of scope' (…so no observable DC behavior changes on merge)

findings.finding: Redefining normalize_outbound to decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) makes the live DC send ship rendered wiki on merge of THIS story, contradicting the plan's own scope boundary and hazard-before-safety ordering. The shared live send path outbound_mapper.py:77 composes the description as normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value)) — it never calls to_wire — so the instant normalize_outbound renders (DC decode_inbound is identity, so normalize_outbound(t) == to_wire(t) == rendered wiki), issue.update(fields=…) begins receiving rendered wiki with no change to outbound_mapper.py:77 at all.
findings.location: Approach (capability, behind the seam): 'normalize_outbound(t) = decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) … (no longer identity)'; Scope boundary paragraph
findings.suggested_fix: Keep normalize_outbound as a compare-only normalizer distinct from the wire render (mirroring Cloud's AdfCodec, where normalize_outbound=adf.normalize_description and to_wire=adf.text_to_adf, and 3388's stated design 'the compare still uses normalize_outbound'). Put the MD→wiki render exclusively in to_wire; leave normalize_outbound as today's identity (or a compare-stable form). The codec law then remains a genuine cross-check rather than a tautology, and the send at outbound_mapper.py:77 keeps emitting the non-wire form until 3388 wires to_wire into the send/CREATE path.

A rendering normalize_outbound/to_wire will fail test_wiki_normalize_is_identity, test_wiki_codec_wire_shape_and_decode_are_the_plain_string, and test_non_string_values_pass_through_untouched.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 7 ('existing tests staying green')

The plan changes WikiTextCodec.to_wire and WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound from identity to a rendering codec, but its affected-test inventory names only test_rich_text_codec.py:163 (the law test) and asserts other existing tests 'stay green'. Three existing tests in the same file directly pin the identity behavior being replaced and are omitted: test_wiki_codec_wire_shape_and_decode_are_the_plain_string (:244), test_wiki_normalize_is_identity (:251), and test_non_string_values_pass_through_untouched (:189-190, parametrized over WikiTextCodec).
findings.location: Scope ('tests/ — segmenting/arrow/table/law corpus tests') and AC final line ('the live send sites ... are unchanged ... verified by their existing tests staying green')
